commentary: Iron ore futures moved downwards aŌer a higher opening today, with the most-traded contract I2601 closing at 800 yuan, down 0.12% from the previous trading day. Traders showed moderate willingness to sell; steel mills adopted a cauƟous wait-and-see approach and purchased as needed. Market trading acƟvity was moderate. In Shandong, mainstream transacƟon prices for old-grade PB ﬁnes were 790-795 yuan/mt, down 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday; new-grade PB ﬁnes traded near 780 yuan/mt. In Tangshan, transacƟon prices for PB ﬁnes were 795-800 yuan/mt, down 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday. The US Fed cut interest rates by 25 bps as expected, leading to a short-term exhausƟon of macro tailwinds and a marginal weakening in market senƟment, which exerted some pressure on futures. However, from an industrial fundamental perspecƟve, apparent demand for the ﬁve major steel products conƟnued to recover slightly this week. Although total inventory increased slightly WoW, rebar inventory has already reached an inﬂecƟon point and begun destocking. The recovery in ﬁnished steel demand is providing a ﬂoor support for iron ore prices, and futures have shown strong resistance to declines. Considering that some steel mills sƟll have restocking needs ahead of the holiday, overall raw material consumpƟon is expected to grow, and ore prices are likely to stabilize and rebound in the near term.
